Flag outlying monthly vaccination counts

Source: R/flag_outliers.R
flag_outliers.Rd

For every unit of the chosen level and every vaccine, the monthly number of vaccinated children is compared only with the other months of that same unit. Five standard statistical rules are computed side by side and every statistic is returned, so the reason a month is flagged can be audited. Only base R is used.

Usage

flag_outliers(
  data,
  level,
  vaccine = NULL,
  months = 1:12,
  min_methods = 2,
  flagged_only = TRUE,
  k_iqr = 1.5,
  z_cut = 3,
  mad_cut = 3.5,
  alpha = 0.05,
  min_diff = 20,
  min_months = 5,
  accent = FALSE
)

Arguments

data

Dataframe, the DHIS2 immunization dataframe (as passed to vaccine_sums).

level

The aggregation level of interest, specified as in vaccine_sums: Country, Province, District, Aire, Fosa, Antenne, or a combination such as c(Antenne, District).

vaccine

Character vector of vaccine names (see vaccine_sums). NULL (default) uses every vaccine the package knows.

months

Integer vector of months to consider. Months in which no unit reports any dose of the vaccine are ignored. Default 1:12.

min_methods

Number of rules (out of 5) that must flag a month for flagged to be TRUE. Default 2.

flagged_only

If TRUE (default) only flagged months are returned; if FALSE every unit-vaccine-month is returned with its statistics.

k_iqr

Multiplier of the IQR fences. Default 1.5.

z_cut

Cutoff of the leave-one-out z-score. Default 3.

mad_cut

Cutoff of the modified z-score. Default 3.5.

alpha

Significance level of the GESD test. Default 0.05.

min_diff

Minimum absolute difference from the unit's median for a rule to flag a month. Default 20.

min_months

Minimum number of reporting months needed to assess a unit. Default 5.

accent

Passed to vaccine_sums. Default FALSE (data already cleaned).

Value

A dataframe with one row per unit, vaccine and month containing: the unit column(s), vaccine, month, value (monthly count), the series statistics (n, median, mean_other, sd_other, q1, q3, iqr, mad, medcouple), ratio_median (value / median), each rule's statistic and limits (iqr_lower, iqr_upper, adjbox_lower, adjbox_upper, z_loo, mod_z, gesd_stat, gesd_crit), one logical flag per rule (flag_iqr, flag_adjbox, flag_zscore, flag_mad, flag_gesd), n_flags, flagged and direction ("high", "low" or NA). Sorted by n_flags and relative distance from the median.

Details

Monthly counts are the differences between consecutive cumulative totals from vaccine_sums, so the columns summed for each vaccine are exactly those used for the coverage computation.

The rules, all applied to the unit's own monthly series:

  • iqr: Tukey fences, Q1 - kIQR and Q3 + kIQR (k = 1.5).

  • adjbox: adjusted boxplot of Hubert and Vandervieren (2008). The fences are skewed with the medcouple, which suits count data that are not symmetric.

  • zscore: leave-one-out z-score. The month is compared with the mean and SD of the unit's other months, so an extreme value cannot inflate the SD and hide itself (|z| > 3).

  • mad: modified z-score of Iglewicz and Hoaglin, 0.6745 * (x - median) / MAD (|M| > 3.5).

  • gesd: generalized extreme Studentized deviate test of Rosner (1983), which finds up to several outliers while controlling the type I error (alpha = 0.05).

A month is flagged by a rule when it is outside that rule's limits and at least min_diff away from the unit's median (so tiny fluctuations in small units are ignored). The final flagged column is TRUE when at least min_methods rules agree.

References

Hubert M, Vandervieren E (2008). An adjusted boxplot for skewed distributions. Computational Statistics and Data Analysis 52:5186-5201.

Iglewicz B, Hoaglin D (1993). How to detect and handle outliers. ASQC Quality Press.

Rosner B (1983). Percentage points for a generalized ESD many-outlier procedure. Technometrics 25:165-172.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
flag_outliers(ri, District, vaccine = c("DTC1", "Pneumo13"), months = 1:9)
flag_outliers(ri, c(Antenne, District), months = 1:9, min_methods = 3)
flag_outliers(ri, District, vaccine = "BCG", flagged_only = FALSE)
} # }
